record.paper_title: Revisiting the foundations of the quantum theory of atoms in molecules: Some open problems
record.context_brief: Extending density-topology conjectures beyond point nuclei
record.original_question: Can the critical-distance explanation of topological-atom naturalness be extended from point-charge Coulomb external potentials to larger classes of external potentials, such as finite-nucleus models or other marginal modifications, by proving that the topology of the one-electron density is independent of those marginal changes?

evidence.quote: Also, it is interesting to extend the conjecture to a larger class of external potentials, e.g. those derived from the finite nucleus models [76], since the topology of the one-electron density is probably independent from marginal modifications of the external potential (for a similar proposal see [23]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $V_{\rm ext}:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}$ be an external one-body potential acting on a non-relativistic $N$-electron system with Hamiltonian
$$H[V_{\rm ext}] = \sum_{i=1}^{N}\Big(-\tfrac{1}{2}\Delta_{i} + V_{\rm ext}(\mathbf{r}_i)\Big) + \sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac{1}{|\mathbf{r}_i-\mathbf{r}_j|}.$$
For a (ground-state) wavefunction $\Psi$ of $H[V_{\rm ext}]$, let $\rho_{V_{\rm ext}}(\mathbf{r})$ denote the associated one-electron density. Define the topology of $\rho$ as the homeomorphism class of the gradient-vector-field decomposition of $\mathbb{R}^3$ into basins of attraction of the maxima of $\rho$ (equivalently, the CW-structure determined by the critical points of $\rho$ and their stable/unstable manifolds, in the sense of the Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules).

The standard "point-nucleus" Coulomb external potential associated with nuclear positions $\{\mathbf{R}_a\}_{a=1}^{M}$ and charges $\{Z_a\}$ is
$$V^{\rm pt}_{\rm ext}(\mathbf{r}) = -\sum_{a=1}^{M}\frac{Z_a}{|\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{R}_a|}.$$
A "finite-nucleus" external potential is one of the form
$$V^{\rm fn}_{\rm ext}(\mathbf{r}) = -\sum_{a=1}^{M} Z_a\,(\mu_a * |\mathbf{r}|^{-1})(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{R}_a),$$
where each $\mu_a$ is a compactly supported (e.g. uniform-ball or Gaussian) probability measure modeling the spatial extent of nucleus $a$; more generally, a marginal modification of $V^{\rm pt}_{\rm ext}$ is any potential $V_{\rm ext}=V^{\rm pt}_{\rm ext}+W$ where $W$ is bounded and supported in small neighborhoods of the nuclei.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following conjecture: for every set $\{(\mathbf{R}_a,Z_a)\}$ of nuclear data and every marginal modification $W$ as above (in particular, for every finite-nucleus potential $V^{\rm fn}_{\rm ext}$), the topology of the ground-state one-electron density $\rho_{V^{\rm pt}_{\rm ext}}$ coincides with the topology of $\rho_{V^{\rm pt}_{\rm ext}+W}$. Equivalently, identify a critical-distance/perturbative criterion on $W$ guaranteeing that the QTAIM critical-point structure (number, type, and connectivity of nuclear, bond, ring, and cage critical points) of the one-electron density is invariant under the replacement $V^{\rm pt}_{\rm ext}\mapsto V^{\rm pt}_{\rm ext}+W$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published proof or disproof of the conjectured topological invariance of the one-electron density under finite-nucleus or other marginal modifications of the external potential was located. The QTAIM literature describes the critical-point structure and notes sensitivity of the topology to relativistic and computational details, but no general theorem of independence under such marginal modifications has been established, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Molecular QTAIM Topology Is Sensitive to Relativistic Effects
status_evidence.snippet: Studies show QTAIM topology can change under relativistic and other modifications, indicating no general invariance theorem.
status_evidence.claim: The topology of the one-electron density is known to be sensitive to certain modifications of the Hamiltonian, suggesting the conjectured invariance under finite-nucleus modifications is non-trivial and not established.

status_evidence.title: On Quantum Chemical Topology
status_evidence.snippet: General review of QTAIM and density topology, with no theorem on invariance under marginal external-potential modifications.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of quantum chemical topology do not report a proof of topology independence under finite-nucleus or other marginal external-potential changes.
